text: Meridian Outfitters' environment pulled together everything this course taught, chapter by chapter, instead of introducing anything genuinely new. This review walks the same four capstone lessons back through the chapters they came from — identity, compute, storage, networking, the CLI, monitoring, and cost — to show exactly how each piece fit into one real, administered environment rather than a set of disconnected topics.

Chapter 1's identity rules showed up directly as meridian-app1's IAM role instead of a hardcoded access key. Chapter 2's EC2 fundamentals put two instances into two different tiers with two different reachability stories. Chapter 3's S3 and EBS content gave both tiers shared storage plus a snapshot for backup. Chapter 4's VPC and subnetting is what made a public tier and a private tier possible at all, and gave Lesson 31's entire incident a clear, checkable cause.

Chapter 5's CLI wasn't its own isolated topic by the time Lesson 29 arrived — it had already become the thread running through every other chapter's commands, and it's the reason Lesson 31's four-question diagnosis could run in under a minute instead of hours of guessing. CloudWatch and CloudTrail, both from Chapter 6, caught the CPU problem and would have shown exactly who launched the wrong instance into the wrong subnet, and from which credentials. Chapter 7's budget alert is what catches a cost problem on day nineteen of the month instead of on an invoice thirty days later.

Eight chapters, one command line running underneath all of them: create-vpc, run-instances, create-role, put-metric-alarm, create-budget, describe-instances. Every one of those belongs to a different chapter's subject matter, and every one of them is also just an aws call with a service, an action, and a handful of flags — which is the entire point Chapter 5 was making.

That's the whole course — from retiring the root account on day one to deploying, securing, monitoring, troubleshooting, and cost-managing a real multi-tier AWS environment end to end, the way a working SysOps administrator actually would. Course complete. Next up in this path: Cloud Networking, Identity & Security.
